answers.explanation: The passage is about the craze for new and quaint clothes among fashionable people, so Fashion craze is the suitable title.
Swallowing their own phlegm and humouring their children means parents overcame their pride or prejudice to accept the children's demands.
The passage says youths make new clothes for festivals, ceremonies, honouring dead colleagues, weddings and matriculation ceremonies.
The passage says parents, plagued by school fees, endure hardship to humour their children's need for special clothes.
The passage says the subtle cause of high blood pressure is the problem of choosing what to wear.
The writer says delinquency is a weapon forged by adults against young people, born of envy and intolerance, so it is unfair to juveniles.
The passage says status offences can be committed only by people in particular stations of life, so they apply to specified classes of people.
The writer says these offences preserve good things of life for the exclusive enjoyment of adults, so adults want the drink for themselves.
The passage says if the world changed overnight, delinquency would refer to many of the adult actions committed now.
The passage says adults should expect a raw deal in return, meaning young people would retaliate against them.
The passage says the element of luck plays a dominant role in Ludo, so it is more a game of luck than of skill.
The passage says two players with equal luck may fare differently depending on skill, so equal skill makes them fare equally.
The passage describes ones and twos as low and sixes and fives as the high throws, so threes and fours are medium throws.
The passage says consistent sixes and fives will help a player home all four counters before the others.
The passage says skill lets a player use his figures efficiently, which is the advantage skill gives.
The passage says farming is the most important aspect of agriculture.
The passage says farming is regarded as the mainstay of the economy in many parts of the world today.
The passage calls for financing through loans and institutions and for modernizing the farming system, so C is the best option.
The passage says farmers lack a good place to store their crops, which is why most are destroyed.
The passage says objects are removed from their natural or proper environments and put into museums, which makes museums artificial.
The main functions of museums named in the passage are preservation, presentation and assemblage, so generation is not one.
The passage says museums are the institution one goes to for evidence of material culture more than any other.
For transmitting expresses the function of museums, not their artificial character.
The passage means museums are a ready example of material culture, the first to come to mind.

A shadow is the absence of light, so the opposite is rays.
To be locked up means to be confined, so its opposite is released.
Courageously means bravely, so its opposite is timidly.
Free to leave means at liberty to leave.
To surrender means to give up something, which is closest to give up.
An animated discussion is a lively one.
Niggardly means stingy, which is closest to miserly.
Popularity beginning to decline means beginning to wane.
To look out for someone means to watch for them.
A prosecution witness is a witness for the government.
To snowball means to grow rapidly, so the takings grew.
To nip something in the bud means to cut it short at an early stage.
To make good a promise means to fulfil it.
The robber's warning What it means look out, to be alert to danger.
Tell-tale signs are revealing marks that give evidence of what happened.
To come to grief means to come to a bad end.
Fired here means dismissed, so they got themselves sacked from their jobs.
To look off means to begin, so the new system began this school year.
To buy an idea means to accept it.
A surplus means more than is needed, so it is more than enough.
A lucrative profession brings plenty of profit.
Off the record means not intended for publication.
To be up against competition means to be faced with it.
To go back on one's word means to fail to keep one's promise.
To respect someone is to look up to them.
Hesitant to start means reluctant to start.
Unimportant matters are trivial matters.
To take the audience down memory lane means to recall events from the past.
To hold out an olive branch means to offer peace.
To lose one's tongue means to be unable to speak, and the passage gives shyness as the reason.
To cook the books means to falsify the accounts for one's advantage.
Herculean means extremely demanding.
A story that is hard to believe is incredible.
To administer a test means to give it.
Ostensibly means apparently, as he appeared to be trying to keep order.
Thieves who enter a house break in.
Counsel after a guilty verdict made a plea for mitigation before sentence was passed.
The correct spelling is trafficking.
A tag after a negative suppose is positive, so did you?
Oranges are countable, so a few left is correct.
For ages with a present result takes the present perfect, haven't had.
To put up with noise means to tolerate it.
Met one another is the correct reciprocal pronoun for two people.
News is uncountable, so any news is correct, and the question uses is there.
To be entitled to a holiday means to have a right to it.
To recite by heart means to recite from memory.
To withhold assent means to refuse approval.
Gone are the days when people used to enjoy patronage.
Burial rites is the plural form needed.
To seize something means to take it by force, which fits the officer's action.
To take a statement literally is to take it at its exact meaning.
High morale means high spirit, which was an advantage.

Suspects were paraded in front of the victim.
Had better is the correct modal expression.

Approaching the end of the programme is the correct sense.
After saw him, the bare infinitive leap is correct.

Enjoyed ourselves is the correct reflexive form.
The lights went off, meaning they went out.
The past tense and past participle of hang for a picture is hung.
Lend is the correct verb for giving a pen temporarily to someone.
Come with you means to accompany you.
Laid is the past tense of lay, which takes an object such as eggs.
